source_work: Noah Webster, An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828)
rights_basis: The original 1828 dictionary text is public domain; only its historical definitions and examples are transcribed, not website editorial material.
transcription_source: Internet Archive volume 2 OCR, cross-checked against clean Webster transcriptions; original OCR is retained unchanged.
selection_method: Selected the first four exact KJV-used S headwords in alphabetical order from the unreviewed high/medium OCR queue. This is a targeted OCR queue, not a claim that all Webster entries have been reviewed.
review_method: Cross-checked all retained definitions and examples against the clean transcriptions and surrounding original OCR, restored omitted SCHOOL noun senses, removed neighboring entries and running headers, corrected broken words and numbering, retained cited authors, and expanded parts of speech for display. Source spans are one-based lines in the hash-verified OCR file.
review_scope: Definitions and examples only. Damaged multilingual etymology for SCHOOL and SCORCH is omitted rather than guessed; their original OCR remains available. All seven SCHOOL noun senses, both SCHOOL verb senses, both SCORCH transitive senses, and its intransitive definition are retained.

entries.review_note: Kept two adjective senses; excluded the following SCABBEDNESS entry that the base import had merged. Accent mark follows the clean transcription.
The base noun entry stopped after ten lines of etymology. Restored the seven noun senses at OCR lines 173453-173530 and retained both verb senses. Excluded SCHOOL-BOY and other compound headwords.
Preserved historical wording, including mungy straw and the cold-weather example, as found in both sources; did not modernize these phrases.
Removed the following SEATING and SEAVES entries that had been merged into SEATED.
